generatedProse.concept-context: Psychology work swings between the two modes all the time. Designing a study starts divergent: you brainstorm the ways a question could be tested, including awkward ones. Then it turns convergent: you weigh the designs against what is feasible and ethical, and choose. Running both at once, judging each design as it occurs, tends to leave you with the first safe option and little else.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two psychology students plan the same essay, with twenty minutes before a seminar.

Tom picks an argument straight away and starts writing, judging each sentence as it comes. Twenty minutes later there is half a paragraph, each line reworked twice. Tom ran both modes at once, generating and judging in the same breath, so little was generated and less survived.

Amara spends the first ten minutes listing every angle on the question, good and bad, without stopping to judge. Then, in the second ten, she reads the list, crosses out the weak ones, and picks the two that connect into an argument. Generating first and choosing second gave her more to work with, and a stronger choice.

Both had the same twenty minutes. Only Amara kept the two modes apart, which let the ideas flow and then settle.
generatedProse.summary: In psychology, creative thinking uses two modes: divergent thinking generates possibilities, and convergent thinking narrows them to the strongest. You can now tell the two apart, see why generating should come before judging, and choose the mode that fits the stage you are at. The next lesson looks at the barriers that stop this working, and how to move past them.

check.body: In the worked example, what did Amara do that let the ideas flow?

items.text: She generated a list of angles first, without judging, then chose afterwards.
She started writing the argument straight away and judged each line.
She spent the whole time polishing one sentence.
She waited for a single good idea to arrive.

feedback.correct: That's right. Amara generated first and judged second, keeping the two modes apart.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for the move that separated generating from judging.
feedback.incorrectFinal: The ideas flowed because Amara generated a list first and judged afterwards. Writing straight away, polishing one line, or waiting for one idea all collapse the two modes together.
